implementation.legacy_semantics: one exact executable value, no arguments, inherited cwd and environment, inherited stdio, synchronous status only

command.argv: ordered UTF-8 arguments preserved as distinct values with argv[0] equal to executable identity
command.environment: inherit nothing by default; pass only policy-approved keys with explicit values

stdio.stdin_close: close after input is written or immediately when no input is supplied
stdio.capture_overflow: terminate child and report process.output_limit_exceeded with bounded retained bytes

lifecycle.cancellation: request graceful termination, wait bounded grace, then force termination

terminal.detection: query each inherited or streamed endpoint independently
terminal.size: optional positive columns and rows from the attached terminal endpoint

authority.executable_rule: exact executable identity must be allowed before spawn
authority.argv_rule: argument count, origins, and structural policy are checked separately from executable identity
authority.cwd_rule: resolved cwd must remain inside an allowed root
authority.environment_rule: inheritance and each key are independently authorized; values never grant authority
authority.process_control_rule: caller wait, graceful termination, force termination, timeout handling, cancellation, and resource-limit ceilings are independently authorized
authority.runtime_cleanup_rule: process-control denial blocks only the caller-requested operation; runtime supervision remains mandatory, closes pipes and reaps every child, and handle abandonment triggers bounded graceful-then-forced termination
authority.signals_rule: signal subscription and each portable signal send are independently authorized
authority.stdio_rule: stdin, stdout, and stderr modes are authorized independently before spawn
authority.terminal_rule: terminal detection, size queries, and terminal inheritance or streaming are independently authorized

audit.denied_rule: record denied dimensions and stable identities without spawning or recording argument, environment, or stdin values

resource_limits.default_rule: omitted values use finite published defaults; process_control authority may lower defaults but never remove a bound
resource_limits.authority_rule: process_control authority sets a finite ceiling per supported limit; a request above its ceiling is denied before spawn

failures.exceeded: terminate and clean up with process.resource_limit_exceeded and the exceeded limit name

asserts: argument boundaries, ordering, spaces, and Unicode survive without shell parsing
every authority dimension has an allowed path and a denied path that cannot perform its protected action
audit reports approved keys and redacts environment, argument, and stdin values
capture is bounded and overflow terminates the child with a stable output-limit outcome and diagnostic
supported limits use finite defaults and authority ceilings while invalid, unauthorized, unsupported, and exceeded limits fail closed
shell metacharacters remain one literal argument
portable signal outcome is distinct from exit code
terminal detection, size, and color policy are explicit
timeout and explicit cancellation have distinct bounded graceful-then-forced paths and outcomes

migration.compatibility: run_status(command: string) remains a legacy synchronous status helper; it does not satisfy or implicitly opt into the structured Process v1 contract
